You are a creative director who has coached many winning hackathon demos and a visual designer. Read-only: do not edit files. Judge the current product UI as the jury (Lio, an AI procurement startup) will see it in a 3-minute live demo, and propose the overall layout and visual style that make the story land in the first 30 seconds and look like a real product.

Context: repo /Users/jonasstenglein/OtherProjects/StartMunichHack/ask-soony. Read docs/challenge.md (judging: pitch that sticks, real business case, technical depth, taste), data/notes/pitch-sun.md (our pitch material, confidential). Screenshots of the current UI: /Users/jonasstenglein/.claude/jobs/3021cc1a/tmp/ui-inbox/*.png and /Users/jonasstenglein/.claude/jobs/3021cc1a/tmp/design/*.png (look at all). Code: web/src/App.tsx, components/*, web/src/index.css (tokens), web/src/lib/api.ts (data).
The story: "Soony's SAP says Saturday; a Korean PDF in the supplier folder says 20,000 game cards arrive Tuesday, after launch; nobody read it." Every number links to the highlighted spot in the source. One tap / a phone call decides; the supplier's real reply lands on the card. Then: "every decision teaches the next one" — an agent writes a routine (shown as an n8n-like flow) that handles the next 3 similar cards on its own; money and plan changes always stay human.

Deliver (under ~700 words):
1. Verdict: does the world map + KPI strip help or hurt the story? Keep, demote (tab/inset), or replace (with what: launch timeline, a single "launch at risk" hero, a feed)?
2. Your recommended top-to-bottom layout for the main screen at 1440 px (ASCII wireframe), designed so the demo's beats (problem → evidence → decision → reply → routine takes over) each have an obvious place on screen and the presenter never hunts.
3. Visual style: keep the current light Linear-like style or change (colour usage for risk, typography scale, density, dark mode?), concrete token-level suggestions using the existing palette (ink/ink-2/ink-3, line, panel, ok blue #1d6fe0, stop red, amber, grey). What makes it feel like a funded startup's product rather than a hackathon dashboard.
4. A "hero moment" visual: how the contradiction (SAP 48,000 Saturday vs document 20,000 Tuesday) should look so it is readable from the back of a room on a projector.
5. Top 5 things to remove or rename.

# Lio Challenge: "Keep the Line Running" (START Hack Munich 2026)

This file is the complete challenge context, compiled from the four official documents Lio provided: the challenge brief, the judging criteria, the deep-dive slides (including speaker notes) and a challenge summary. It describes the problem only. It contains no proposed solution or architecture. Those decisions are open.

> Soony, Popstar Studios and Grand Heist 6 are entirely fictional.
> Use the challenge data only for this hackathon and do not share it outside the team.

---

## 1. Role and framing

- The team plays **Lio**, a young AI startup that has just closed its **first paying customer, Soony**.
- Lio (the real company) runs procurement end to end for 175+ global enterprises (BMW, Siemens, ZEISS, among others) with a multi-agent system of hundreds of specialised AI agents.
- Soony bought "an AI solution to save the launch." **That solution does not exist yet. The team has to build it.**
- Why Soony bought a startup: no time for a tender or a big vendor project. They needed help this weekend. The last three weeks nearly broke their team.
- Sales call: the CPO asked, "Can it chase suppliers for us?" The answer was, "Yes, sort of." The pitch was "an AI workforce that keeps their supply chain running."
- **Soony's ask: "No more surprises."**
- Soony's stated pain: "Suppliers tell us about problems way too late. By then, our launch date is already at risk, and every fix is expensive."
- Quote from Soony: "Our fans have waited years for this game. If it is not on the shelf on Sunday, nobody will remember the game. They will remember that we missed it."

---

## 2. The customer: Soony Interactive GmbH

- A console and games publisher headquartered in **Munich**.
- Releasing **Grand Heist 6**, developed by Popstar Studios. The heist series is back after 13 years. It's the biggest game release of the year.
- **Soony makes nothing itself.** Six suppliers deliver the parts, and every copy is packed at **one site: Soony's distribution center in Hamburg**. There is **no plan B site**.
- From Hamburg, trucks take the boxes to retailers across Europe.

### Key facts

| Fact | Value |
|---|---|
| Launch | **Sunday 22 November 2026, 20:00**. The date cannot move: it's fixed by retail and by pre-orders |
| Trucks to retail | Leave Hamburg from Sunday 20:00. **Whatever is not on them misses launch day** |
| Pre-orders | 487,000 |
| Standard Edition demand (day one) | 640,000 copies |
| Collector's Edition demand | 72,000 copies, **every copy numbered, all pre-ordered** |
| Suppliers | 6 |
| Logistics providers | 4 (ocean, air cargo, a forwarder in India, trucks from Poznań) |
| Distribution center | 1, in Hamburg |
| Packing time left | **30 hours**: Sat 06:00–22:00 and Sun 06:00–20:00. **No night shift** |
| Why so late | The game master was finished late, so the programmed game cards only started arriving three weeks ago |

---

## 3. Situation at kickoff: "80% packed, the last 20% is on you"

| | Standard Edition | Collector's Edition |
|---|---|---|
| Packed at kickoff | 512,000 of 640,000 (80%) | 46,800 of 72,000 (65%) |
| Still to pack | 128,000 | 25,200 |
| Parts per box | 4 | 7 |
| Packing setup | 3 pack lines | 1 manual cell; **all 7 parts must be present at the same time** |
| Hours needed (of 30 left) | 21 | 28 |
| Slack | 9 hours | **2 hours** |
| Rate (derived) | ~6,100 copies/hour | **900 copies/hour; every hour the cell waits for a part costs 900 copies** |

Additional facts:
- **Standard Edition parts:** game card, clear case, cover sleeve, activation code leaflet.
- **Collector's Edition parts:** game card, steel case, collector's box, art book, city map poster, die-cast statue, leaflet.
- The Standard pack lines are **not exclusively reserved** for the launch: Grand Heist 5 reprints still run on the side.
- Standard "is not where the launch breaks, as long as the game cards keep coming."
- Collector's Edition: fans paid for a specific numbered copy, so Soony **cannot ship fewer or swap them**. If one part is missing (e.g. the statue or the art book), the whole cell stands still. Lio calls the Collector's Edition "the real risk this weekend."
- The first 80% took three weeks of firefighting: chasing suppliers by phone, rebooking freight, packing whatever arrived that day. The team is exhausted. The last 20% has no buffer.
- Soony's fear: something in the last 20% blows up and nobody notices until Sunday.
- **Hint from the brief:** "The system says we are fine. My gut says we are not." (*Somebody at Soony, probably. Find out who is right.*)

---

## 4. Supply network

All parts end up in the Hamburg distribution center.

| Supplier | Country | Supplies | Route / transit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hwaseong Memory | South Korea | **70% of game cards** | Sea via Busan (36 days) or air via Incheon |
| Boise Semi | USA | **30% of game cards** | Air via Chicago |
| Guangzhou PackRight | China | Card cases, sleeves, collector's boxes | Sea from Yantian |
| Dongguan Precision Housings | China | Steel cases, **80% of statues**, card cases | Sea from Yantian |
----
# Pitch material (Sun, from the expert round; confidential, local only)

## One line
Ask Soony checks every supplier document against SAP, shows the exact line where they disagree,
and turns each decision you make into a routine that handles the next one. Money always stays human.
Slide tagline: **Every decision teaches the next one.**

## Lead with anchored truth, routines as the climax (jury view)
- Hwaseong: SAP counts 48,000 game cards (PO 4500318735 line 2) for Sat 21 Nov. Korean shipping advice
  (Shipping_advice_020-48113256_4500318735.pdf, p. 1): 28,000 flown, 20,000 arrive Hamburg Tue 24 Nov.
  "Soony's system says Saturday. Hwaseong said Tuesday, in Korean. Nobody read it."
- Then one tap / the phone call, the supplier's real reply appears on the card.
- Climax: PackRight confirmed 4 sleeve POs with the old artwork rev B (ECN rev B -> C, "must not be
  packed"). Decide the first by hand, the agent writes a routine, it handles the other three.

## Quotes (with source)
- Felix (senior buyer, 37s): "has to tell me, before the supplier does, that something will not arrive.
  Otherwise I would not use it."
- Felix (612s): approvers "don't look into the notifications" -> why we call when critical.
- Felix (554s): "at some point they flip the switch and let it run autonomously." -> routines.
- Felix (320s/377s): approval budgets differ per person (10k vs 4M) -> money always human.
- Felix (505s): "sometimes one source is wrong, sometimes the other. In the end I don't care. I want that
  the process works." -> cards end in an action, not a debate.
- Nils (IT, 230-300s): copying supplier receipts into the ERP "for every single order"; errors found
  "weeks or months later".
- Nils (438s): "If uncertain, I would want to know, or if it's a big delivery."
- Nils (740s): "If I can fully trust my data, I would sleep a lot better." (closing line)

## Numbers
- 487,000 pre-orders; still to pack 128,000 Standard + 25,200 Collector's; 30 packing hours left.
- Collector's cell: 2 h slack, every hour waiting for a part costs 900 copies (slides).
- Findings: Hwaseong 20,000 cards after launch; art books really 19,300 not 91,300 (~5,900 CE copies
  short; Nowak offers 8,000 from stock, truck tonight); 5,600 statues failed inspection but booked
  unrestricted (~3,400 CE short); 64,000 rev B sleeves in stock must not be packed; Boise holds 36,000
  cards at its dock until EXW is confirmed.
- Missing: cost per missing copy (Maren). Use as clearly stated assumption if not asked.

## Five hardest questions (short answers)
1. OCR/LLM misreads? No number reaches a card without an anchor in the source (page/row/word box shown
   highlighted); disagreement is shown, never resolved silently; maths is code; nothing goes out or costs
   money without a click.
2. Routine is wrong? Recipe in plain blocks, compiled by us, sandbox (no network/files), test run on the
   live inbox first, each card once, every action logged under its name, one switch off. Only free
   messages are automatic; money and plan changes always come to a person.
3. Different from Lio / Zapier? Zapier moves fields between systems that work; our problem is the gap
   between them (PDFs, scans, Korean mail). Lio runs procurement up to the PO; we cover PO to dock where
   SAP is blind. A layer that plugs into Lio.
4. Customer #2? Nothing Soony-specific in code; the anchor index runs on any files; routines are learned
   from each customer's own decisions.
5. What did Soony tell you? Felix and Nils quotes above.

## Business
- Number: copies that would miss launch day, caught days before the dock (20,000 game cards, ~5,900 +
  ~3,400 Collector's copies).
- Pricing line: platform fee per connected ERP (~EUR 3-5k/month) + per watched supplier (~EUR 100-200);
  for Soony ~EUR 5k/month, less than one day of air freight. Next ten customers: Lio's customers with
  physical inbound parts, sold as an add-on.

## Demo hygiene
- Reset state before the demo (scripts/demo_cards.py --reset); no duplicate routines.
- Deadlines like "decide by Sun 10:00" are past at 14:00: show a replay chip or move deadlines.
- Avoid: narrating the map, staged test calls, too many channels. Show one alert path.

content.text:
**Verdict:** the jury sees a map and two KPI tiles that don't agree with the card. The story is on screen, but it sits in a narrow right column.

## 1. Map and KPI strip: demote both

The map takes 60% of the screen and tells nobody anything. It's a stock "supply chain" visual, your pitch notes already say not to narrate it, and the supplier labels overlap ("Dongguan Precision Housings / Guangzhou PackRight / Pune Diecast Works"). It also turns the problem card into a sidebar.

The KPI strip actively hurts. On screen it reads "Standard 32,000 at risk" next to a card that says 20,000. It also shows "Collector's · On track · 0 at risk", while your pitch calls Collector's "the real risk this weekend" (art books ~5,900 short, statues ~3,400 short). "−18 min slack" doesn't explain itself, "Game Ca…" is cut off, and "checked 8 h ago" undercuts the word "Watching". A juror who reads the top-left first gets a contradiction you didn't intend.

**Replace both with a launch timeline**: one horizontal band from today to Sunday 20:00. Each shipment is a dot, and the launch is a hard red vertical line. Hwaseong's 20,000 lands to the right of that line, after launch. That shows "arrives after launch" before you say a word, and it is the only chart the story needs. Move the map to a "Network" tab.

## 2. Layout at 1440 px


## 3. Visual style

- **Stay light.** Projectors wash out dark UIs and grey-on-dark text. The Linear-like base is right.
- **Ration red.** Right now red is everywhere: border, number, recommendation box, map route, strip. Use `stop` only for things past the launch line (the late quantity and date, the timeline dot, the launch line). Make the recommendation box neutral: `panel` background with a 1 px `line` border and the cost as an ink chip. Use `warn` amber only for "short but recoverable". `ok` blue is for actions only, never for status.
- **Add one more token.** Something like `--color-auto: #7c3aed` (or a teal) marks routine work, so "the agent did this" reads differently from "you did this".
- **Typography scale:** 12 / 14 / 16 / 20 / 28 / 64. One display size, for the hero numbers. Labels at 12 px uppercase with +0.04em tracking in `ink-3`. Card titles at 20/600. Drop the 14 px grey body copy under the recommendation.
- **Density:** fewer boxes. Today it's a card inside a box inside a box. Use one surface per card, separated by 24 px whitespace and hairline dividers.
- **What reads as a funded product:** consistent nouns, no truncation, no internal IDs (CMP-GAM-001), live relative times ("2 min ago"), and a real empty state, which you already have and is good. A tiny "source-anchored" mark (a small doc icon plus page number) next to every number makes the trust claim visible.
